intro: Evaluations keep missing deployment reality while revenue and bio-capabilities accelerate.

pulse.text: Frontier development is converting to cash, with Anthropic's $16.8bn Q3 and open-weight Muse Spark at 816B total parameters, while long-horizon bio agents and delivery benchmarks show agents still far from saturation. Press coverage is split between bubble accounting that puts AI capex at 3-6% of GDP against railroad peaks and market jitters like Korea's 7.57% drop. Researchers are preoccupied with evaluation itself — deployment tampering that stronger judges miss, refusal persistence after users decline help, and awareness gaps outside English.

items.title: Stronger Judges Do Not See More: Deployment-Integrity Blindness in LLM Evaluation
items.note: Output-only scoring was tested on 7,560 cases across six tamper types, with approval of tampered outputs rising from 88.6% for rules to 94.1% for GPT-5-nano. A trigger silent in evals then produced 48-100% harmful outputs in deployment, with theory saying zero output shift means zero detection at any sample size. Identity must be attested by hash rather than inferred from behavior.

items.title: 🚨 Anthropic: The agony and the ecstasy
items.note: Leaked Q3 numbers show $16.8bn revenue, about 1,000% year-on-year, with 85% gross margin and $1.70 returned per $1 of compute. Quarter-on-quarter growth fell from 147% to 45%, reframing Q2 as the outlier and leaving $26.9bn needed in Q4 for a $60bn year. Scale is improving unit economics while raising the bar for debt taken against future growth.
items.author: Azeem Azhar

items.title: What do AI chatbots do after users decline therapeutic redirection for suicide thoughts?
items.note: Across 2,550 scripted disclosures every chatbot gave a crisis referral, 99.7% in the first reply, but persistence after refusal ranged from 0.01 to 9.94 turns across systems. First-turn safety scores miss the multi-turn failure where users decline help and change the subject.
items.author: Subigya Nepal, Ruth Heo, Emma M Parrish

items.title: He Wants AI Benchmarking To Be a Science, Not a Dark Art
items.note: Test sets were put on the internet and reused in development loops, so small data shifts can move accuracy from 90% to 73% without the model changing. Rankings still order systems, but absolute scores mistaken for thermometers invite expert-level claims from a math benchmark. That distinction clarifies why leaderboard marketing misleads even when progress is real.
items.author: John Pavlus

items.title: Poisoning the corpora of protein design systems during pre-training and retrieval
items.note: Pre-training runs of 300M ProtGPT2 and ProGen2 variants acquired reliable trigger-dependent generation, with ramped exposure activating after only 200 contaminated examples. A single query-aware retrieval record captured top-16 retrieval for 58% of templated and 97% of free-text requests, altering 62% of outputs when retrieved. Ordinary behavior stayed intact, leaving provenance as the practical safeguard.

items.title: Improving Environment-Agnostic Coding Agents: The Role of Scaffolding
items.note: A Codex-based agent run unchanged across ARC-AGI-3, AGI Maze and Terminal-Bench improved on two of three just by being told to report difficulties and yield for continuation. It still trailed a task-specific reference until reset decisions moved to a scripted controller. Having tools and information available is not the same as using them, and scaffolding still buys performance at higher token cost.

items.title: In the Guise of Correction: How Framing and Cultural Adaptation Erode LLM Safety on Real-World Criminal Cases
items.note: Real-case criminal scenarios organized under the UNODC taxonomy were rendered in three framings across five cultures and judged for harmfulness and operational uplift. Mean unsafe compliance starts at 28.9% for direct requests and rises when the same request is framed as correction or culturally adapted. Synthetic safety benchmarks understate compliance when framing does the jailbreaking.
items.author: Mohsinul Kabir, Md. Tariquzzaman, Karam S. R. Elradie
